capability.summary: Run a local Vitest suite once with its JSON reporter
capability.description: Runs exactly `vitest run --reporter=json` from the supplied directory, or from the absolute parent of a supplied file, with a 180-second timeout. Vitest executes project configuration, setup files, and tests; the wrapper reports the process result in a JSON envelope and treats exit codes 0 and 1 as completed runs.
capability.problem_space: One-shot execution of an existing Vitest test suite with the built-in JSON reporter. It is not Jest or npm-script execution, watch mode, test authoring, coverage generation, dependency installation, linting, or a sandbox for untrusted tests.

env_requirements: project Vitest configuration and runtime dependencies discoverable from the resolved cwd
constraint.io_signature: Input: required proj_dir string at CLI position 1; an existing directory is cwd, while an existing file selects its absolute parent. Executes `vitest run --reporter=json`. Output: one JSON execution envelope containing the parsed reporter payload when either captured stream is valid JSON, otherwise raw streams.
accepted_inputs: an existing directory for a configured local Vitest project
an existing file whose parent directory should be used as the Vitest project cwd
constraint.output_shape: Vitest exit 0 or 1: {status: "success", tool: "vitest", target: string, exit_code: 0|1, result: any JSON value|null, stdout: string|null, stderr: string|null}, wrapper exit 0. The helper attempts JSON parsing of nonempty stdout first and then stderr; when parsing succeeds result holds that value and stdout is null. Other Vitest exits use the same keys with status="tool_error" and propagate that exit code. Missing target/executable or timeout emits {status: "error", tool: "vitest", message: string} and exits 2/3/4. Missing argument writes usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON.
limitations: executes arbitrary project configuration, setup files, transforms, and test code with the wrapper process permissions; tests may write files, spawn processes, or access the network

the plain string proj_dir contract accepts either an existing directory or an existing file; automatic file-artifact binding does not infer a directory, and a file is converted to its absolute parent cwd
fixed run mode and JSON reporter expose no test-name, file-pattern, coverage, pool, watch, update-snapshot, or passthrough CLI controls
exit code 1, normally test failures, is wrapped as status=success; callers must inspect exit_code and the reporter result
uses a fixed 180-second timeout and captures untruncated stdout/stderr in memory; JSON parsing accepts either stdout or stderr

output_contract.description: JSON execution envelope for `vitest run --reporter=json`, containing exit code, parsed reporter payload when available, and otherwise raw stdout/stderr.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: run a Vitest test suite once
negative_intents: run Jest or an npm test script
